- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Line or code reference: 1410 (`_tmp_output_first_nonempty_line=...`), 1685 (retry-loop short-circuit using same variable)
  Problem: The capture happens inside the per-attempt loop but uses a non-local bash variable with `(...) || true` that can leave the prior-iteration value on empty-output runs; the refusal short-circuit and validator both read it without resetting.
  Why it fails at runtime: On a later retry where `grep -m1` produces no nonempty line, a stale refusal string from a previous attempt can falsely trigger `editor_refused.flag` (and `EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL=true`), causing the fallback path even on a valid structured summary that merely quotes a refusal example deeper in the body. The dedicated test added in this PR exercises the contract but does not cover empty-output reuse across retries.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 10542-10557 (the `_std_cached_head_sha` extraction + conditional `jq -cn` that builds `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED`)
  Problem: When GraphQL returns `head_sha: null` / empty / whitespace the `if $hs != ""` branch omits the `sha` key entirely; the seeded JSON is then asymmetric depending on whether GraphQL or the later REST payload seeded it.
  Why it fails at runtime: The standalone-stall `retrigger_review` guard (and the `blank-head_branch` in-flight check) depends on a reliable `head.sha` in cache. If the REST refetch fails (as the new test forces), the guard silently falls back to an incomplete payload, allowing an empty-commit push to race an in-flight `workflow_dispatch` review run. The added test only checks for absence of push; it does not assert the JSON shape or that a subsequent poll would still recognize the run.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: agents.md
  Line or code reference: 263 (new `PR_PROCESSED_ALERT_LEVEL` table row)
  Problem: The description says "`PR processed: #N` DEBUG ping" while the actual workflow and runbook now default to and document `SILENT`; the entry was added in this forward-merge but the surrounding paragraph was not synchronized.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators relying on `agents.md` for the review-pipeline contract will mispredict Telegram volume (expecting DEBUG pings on every successful iteration). No functional breakage, but documentation drift violates the "lockstep literals" contract enforced by the test suite for refusal and noop markers.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
